name: Shore
tagline: UW-Madison's 1990s persistent object repository whose storage manager became a standard research engine.
description: SHORE (Scalable Heterogeneous Object REpository) was a University of Wisconsin-Madison project led by Michael Carey, David DeWitt and colleagues as the successor to the EXODUS storage manager. It aimed to be a persistent object system for CAD, GIS, persistent programming languages and multimedia, adding typed objects, multi-language access, a Unix-like namespace and a Unix-compatible interface on top of a layered architecture with 'value-added servers'. The full system was described at SIGMOD 1994 and released in 1996; official support ended in 1997. Its transactional storage manager (ARIES-style logging and recovery, B+ trees, R* trees, locking) lived on far longer, used by Paradise, PREDATOR, TIMBER, Lambda-DB and many studies, and was eventually replaced by the multi-threaded Shore-MT.
statusNote: Research system (1990s); support ended in 1997 and the storage manager was superseded by Shore-MT.
strengths: Robust ARIES-style transactional storage manager reused by many research systems
B+ tree and R* tree indexes for both conventional and spatial data
Layered design let projects build custom 'value-added servers'
Decades of published results make it a reference baseline
weaknesses: Single-threaded 'green threads' design does not exploit multicore CPUs
Unsupported since 1997; later releases were as-is
Object-repository layers were deprecated long ago
useCases: History of object-oriented and extensible databases
Understanding the lineage of Shore-MT and later research engines
notIdealFor: New research on multicore hardware (use Shore-MT or newer)
